sections.h2: Who do I call about a Hart County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in Munfordville each hold a piece of a Hart County tax bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the assessed value, the sheriff collects the payment, and the county clerk keeps land records and takes over bills left unpaid.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 566, Munfordville, KY 42765, phone (270) 524-2321. The county lists Monday to Friday, 8 to 4.
  • Sheriff: 100 Main Street, Munfordville, phone (270) 524-2341. The county's sheriff page sends owners to hartcountysheriffky.com to pay bills online.
  • County clerk: 200 Main Street, Munfordville, phone (270) 524-2751. Weekday hours run 8 to 4, plus Saturday from 9 to noon.

Under KRS 134.119 the sheriff is the collector for state, county, school and special district taxes. Partial payments are accepted while the bill is still with the sheriff, and a friend, tenant or lender may pay for the owner.

sections.h2: What is Hart County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Cave country in south central Kentucky: that describes Hart County, where 88.3 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census. The county was formed in 1819 from parts of Hardin and Barren counties and covers 418 square miles. It has two incorporated cities, Munfordville, the seat, and Horse Cave, the largest.

The ground shapes the county. A slice of Mammoth Cave National Park lies in the west, and the Fisher Ridge Cave System, mapped to about 125 miles as of 2018, runs beneath Hart County land. An Amish settlement founded in 1989 between Munfordville and Horse Cave numbered 2,486 people in 2020, about 12.9 percent of the population.

The Battle of Munfordville was fought here in 1862. A courthouse fire in January 1928 destroyed some county records, so sellers of older farms who find a gap in their paperwork can ask the county clerk what survives for their parcel.

The 2020 census counted 7,418 households. About 27.4 percent were one-person households, 31.5 percent had children under 18, and 15.9 percent of the 8,816 housing units were vacant. The county sits in the Central time zone, and Wikipedia's county profile marks the northern lines with Hardin and LaRue counties as the Eastern time border. Check which clock a closing office uses before you set a signing time.

sections.h2: How affordable is housing in Hart County?
sections.html:
Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 describe inexpensive housing that owners mostly occupy themselves. Roughly seven in ten homes are owner-occupied, and values sit far below those of the state's metro counties.

Growth between the April 2020 base and the July 2025 estimate came to 4.3 percent. Households average 2.62 people, and 89.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most owners stay put. Education and work figures round out the picture for a listing: 81.2 percent of adults 25 and older finished high school, 12.2 percent hold a bachelor's degree, and 83.7 percent of households have broadband. Census counts 276 employer establishments with 4,073 jobs in 2023, 1,002 veterans, and an 18.0 percent poverty rate.

Retail sales were about $244.8 million in 2022, or $12,492 per resident, and the average worker spends 28.7 minutes getting to a job. Buyers who commute to larger towns accept that drive in exchange for the prices above.

sections.h2: When does a Hart County tax bill become late?
sections.html:
A Hart County bill goes late once December 31 of the assessment year passes. KRS 134.015 sets the calendar.

  • Through November 1: 2 percent off for paying it all.
  • November 2 to December 31: the printed amount.
  • January: add 5 percent.
  • February on: add 10 percent.

The PVA's office can confirm who is listed as owner on January 1, which decides whose name is on the bill. A buyer who closes in spring should expect the first bill under the seller's name and agree at the table who pays it.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hart County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA first, then go to the county board of assessment appeals if the value still looks wrong. Both steps come from KRS 133.120, which the General Assembly amended effective July 15, 2026.

  1. Request a conference at the PVA's office, which may be held by phone if you ask.
  2. If the number stands, file a petition at the clerk's office within one workday after the inspection period closes. Give your reasons, identify the parcel and state the value you believe is right.
  3. Bring proof to the hearing: listings, sales, insurance records, construction cost or loan papers. A petition without facts is denied.

The board sits 25 to 35 days after inspection ends (KRS 133.030) and inspects the property in person on request. Tax is due on your claimed value meanwhile, with any gap billed later.

sections.h2: Can Hart County homeowners get a homestead exemption?
sections.html: Yes. Owners past 65, or classed as totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value of the home they live in for assessment years 2025 and 2026. On the county's $146,000 Census median, that leaves $96,900 taxable. Apply through the Hart County PVA, and tell the office after a sale so the deduction ends at the old address.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when a Hart County house sells?
sections.html:
The debt follows the parcel, since a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 outlasts a change of owner. A buyer's title search will find it.

Ask the sheriff for a payoff figure before the listing goes live. After unpaid claims move to the county clerk, KRS 134.119 adds a collection fee equal to ten percent of the tax plus ten percent of the penalty, and an investor can buy the certificate of delinquency and add interest. Settle the balance at closing by having the title company deduct it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work when a Hart County house sells?
sections.html: The seller pays Kentucky's transfer tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, and the clerk takes it before recording the deed (KRS 142.050). A $146,000 sale produces a $146 tax. The clerk's office at 200 Main Street in Munfordville keeps the county's land records, so call it for the present recording charge.

faqs.q: Who sends property tax bills in Hart County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office mails and collects them. The PVA supplies the assessed value, and the county clerk handles claims the sheriff does not collect. If no bill arrives, call the sheriff at (270) 524-2341.

faqs.q: What is the Hart County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: $49,100 off assessed value for assessment years 2025 and 2026. Owners over 65 or totally disabled apply through the Hart County PVA at (270) 524-2321.

faqs.q: Does paying early save money in Hart County?
faqs.a: Yes. A full payment made by November 1 of the assessment year earns a 2 percent discount. After December 31 the penalties are 5 percent for January and 10 percent later.

faqs.q: Does an assessment appeal delay my Hart County tax payment?
faqs.a: No. While an appeal is pending you pay tax on the value you claim, and any higher final value is billed later with interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hart County house that still owes taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, though the lien stays with the parcel until it is paid. Get a payoff from the sheriff and have the title company pay it from your proceeds.
